messages:
anya: FYI — big EU customer asked for EU-only data residency + ISO27001 clause. Wants go-live in ~8 weeks. How do we prioritize vs other roadmap work? @leila @mike @samir
leila: That's tight. ISO is a heavy lift (audit evidence, policies, controls). GDPR controls (DSR, encryption at rest, DPIAs) are smaller but still non-trivial. Need to know what they mean by 'ISO clause' — certification or contractual commitments?
samir: They said 'ISO or equivalent + data residency'. Willing to sign a 3yr contract if we can guarantee. $$$ is real.
mike: Engineering estimate for a minimal EU-region deployment + routing + deployment configs: 3-5 sprints to be safe (team of 3). ISO prep/audit adds parallel work (docs + controls), maybe another 8-12 weeks ops + legal time.
rachel: Legal: we can do contractual assurances without certified ISO, but customers often want the cert. If they insist on ISO, procurement will push schedule. Also need to check data transfer clauses for backups and logs.
leila: Propose we separate the asks: 1) Data residency (technical and infra) 2) ISO certification (process + audit). We can sequence. Data residency first as it's high impact for sales. ISO can be a pre-agreed roadmap milestone.
anya: Agreed. Can we quickly RICE-score the two options (rough draft) to decide sequencing?
mike: Quick RICE draft (very rough):
```
Feature: EU data residency
Reach: 1 large customer (but bigger market signal)
Impact: 8 (enables contract)
Confidence: 60%
Effort: 40 engineering-weeks
Score ~ (1*8*0.6)/40 = 0.12

Initiative: ISO27001 certification
Reach: multiple enterprise customers (future deals) = 3
Impact: 6
Confidence: 50%
Effort: 100 eng+ops-weeks (docs + remediation + audit)
Score ~ (3*6*0.5)/100 = 0.09
```

mike: Based on that, data residency first.
leila: Those numbers look fine for a quick decision. Caveat: if the customer contract *requires* certified ISO at signature, then sequencing won't help — we must do ISO earlier.
samir: I asked procurement — they prefer a signed contract with a certification timeline. They'll accept a commitment to achieve ISO within 6 months post-signing if we give liquidated-damages-style SLA credits.
anya: OK — proposed decision: prioritize EU data residency implementation now (can_{canary} for this customer), ship a private region config + routing and DSR support. Meanwhile, start ISO gap assessment as parallel smaller project (PM + security) with clear milestones. Contract will include timeline for certification.
leila: For implementation, minimum security checklist before canary: encryption at rest in region, tenant-level key separation (KMS), DSR endpoints, logging with EU-only retention. I can draft control checklist.
anya: Good. Ops-bot, create ticket for EU-region infra and attach security checklist.
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-4721: "EU data residency - canary for ACME corp". Link: https://redwood.internal/INF-4721 :white_check_mark:
security-bot: Security checklist template: https://redwood.internal/security/templates/eu-residency-checklist.md
anya: Launch criteria for canary (proposal): 1) feature works end-to-end for customer in EU region; 2) security checklist items marked 'implemented' and reviewed by @leila; 3) rollback plan + fallback region policy; 4) signed MSA that allows certification timeline. If all green, ship canary to single-customer prod by week 6.
mike: Sounds doable if we scope the canary to a single tenant and avoid full infra autoscaling at first. Need 2 weeks for infra, 2 weeks for integration, 1 week for validation.
rachel: I'll draft the MSA amendment language to allow a certification timeline and SLA credits.
samir: I'll quietly confirm with the buyer that they accept the timeline before we commit publicly.
leila: One more thing — let's track risk scoring for this rollout (data residency risk + legal exposure). I'll add a risk register entry.
anya: Thanks team. I'll update the roadmap board and move EU-data-residency to 'priority: high', ISO certification to 'priority: medium' with clear milestones. Will post a short PRD by EOD. :rocket:
